posts.dek: The passports are back in the drawer and the W jerseys are back on. September 17 brings five games, ten teams, two national TV windows and one final week to sharpen seed lines, rotations and playoff habits.

sections.title: The W comes back all at once
paragraphs: The WNBA returns September 17 with Connecticut at Atlanta, Washington at Chicago, Los Angeles at Dallas, Phoenix at Portland and Las Vegas at Seattle. The first two games tip at 7:30 PM ET, Dallas follows at 8:00, and the late window begins at 10:00.

This is not a normal restart. The regular season ends September 24 and the playoffs begin September 27. That turns every possession into information about seeding, rhythm, workload and which teams can switch back from international basketball fastest.

sections.title: The guide is a dashboard, not a poster
paragraphs: The full watch guide connects to the site's live 2026 standings and game feeds, official team artwork, current Playerpedia rosters and advanced player metrics. Scores, records, streaks, last ten form, PER and true shooting can update without rewriting the story.

It also teaches four things to watch beyond points: the first five minutes after the international break, the possession battle, what happens after a paint touch and which five players a coach trusts to close.

sections.title: Real players only
paragraphs: Player cards use official WNBA headshots when available and real ESPN roster photography as the fallback. Team marks come from the site's existing team artwork feed. No AI generated player images are used in the guide.

posts.dek: One World Cup, sixteen names, three tiers. Jackie Young runs Shak’s All FIBA Starting Five, Gabby Williams brings the havoc, Stewie brings the MVP, Emma Meesseman brings the tournament’s loudest efficiency, and the Bench Mob is loaded enough to start an argument by itself.

sections.title: The five I would actually start
paragraphs: Jackie Young gets the ball first. Her championship game made the case even louder, but the fit is what seals it. Young can organize, defend and score without needing every possession. Gabby Williams gives the backcourt a second creator and the tournament's most disruptive perimeter defender. Leonie Fiebich adds size, rebounding and connective passing on the wing.

Breanna Stewart is the automatic frontcourt choice after another gold medal and a second World Cup MVP. Emma Meesseman gets the final spot because lineup balance matters more to me than copying the official awards sheet. She led the tournament in scoring and efficiency while still creating for teammates. That is too much offense, size and intelligence to leave outside the first five.

sections.title: The Bench Mob would change the game
paragraphs: Trinity San Antonio and Sevgi Uzun give the second unit pressure at both ends. San Antonio led the tournament in steals, while Uzun led it in assists. Angel Reese is there to turn one missed shot into another possession. Xu Han supplies a true interior scorer. Sika Kone brings efficient power, and Ramu Tokashiki gives the group a tournament leading rim protector.

That is the point of a Bench Mob. The second unit should not imitate the starters. It should introduce a new problem. This one can speed the game up, dominate the glass, pound the paint or lock down the rim depending on what the matchup needs.

sections.title: Honorable mention is not a consolation prize
paragraphs: Iyana Martin was brilliant enough to make the official All-Star Five and win Rising Star while carrying Spain to bronze. Steph Talbot did everything for Australia. Nyara Sabally helped Germany make history. Janelle Salaun was central to France's first finals run, and Dorka Juhasz left Berlin averaging a double double.
There was no clean top ten in Berlin. There were too many players with real cases, which is exactly why the honorable mention group belongs on the board instead of disappearing beneath the cut line.

debates: Would you start Emma Meesseman over Iyana Martin if the goal is lineup balance rather than matching FIBA's official five?

foodSegment.title: Shak’s bite: this roster would be rude
foodSegment.script: Jackie organizes it, Gabby wrecks it, Fiebich connects it, Stewie closes it and Emma makes every matchup uncomfortable. Then Trinity, Sevgi, Angel, Xu Han, Sika Kone and Ramu Tokashiki walk in off the bench. That is not a rotation. That is an international problem.

posts.seriesLabel: SNACK SHAK BYTE · FIBA WORLD CUP FINAL
posts.title: One Streak. One Drought. One Trophy: USA vs France for the World
posts.imageAlt: Team USA celebrating the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup championship in Berlin
posts.dek: USA brings 35 straight World Cup wins and a 71 game run across World Cup and Olympic play. France brings the tournament's biggest average scoring margin and its first World Cup final. Paris 2024 was one point. Berlin gets the rematch.

sections.title: Dynasty meets the team with the loudest margin
paragraphs: USA enters the title game with 35 consecutive World Cup wins, four straight World Cup championships and a 71 game winning streak across World Cup and Olympic play. France enters 5 and 0, averaging 96.2 points and winning by 35.6 points per game through the semifinals.
Both teams are unbeaten. Only one arrives with eleven world titles. Only one arrives in its first World Cup final.

sections.title: Paris was one point. Berlin gets the rematch.
paragraphs: The 2024 Olympic gold medal game ended USA 67, France 66. Now Gabby Williams and France get another championship shot at the Americans, while Breanna Stewart and USA try to make a fifth consecutive World Cup title feel inevitable one more time.

debates: Can France's tournament best scoring margin survive USA's depth and late game defense?
Does the pressure sit heavier on the program protecting a 35 game streak or the program playing its first World Cup final?
Which matters more in one game, USA's history or France's current form?

foodSegment.title: One Streak, One Drought, One Trophy
foodSegment.script: USA walks in with 35 straight World Cup wins and four straight titles. France walks in with zero world titles, but also with the bigger scoring margin in Berlin and a first ever trip to the final. Paris 2024 came down to one point. So no, this is not a coronation. It is a rematch with receipts.
